text:
maria: noticing ~18% token/sec drop in prod since 2471120000 merge. p50 fine, p95 and p99 token/sec and queueing delay up. :thinking:
ashwin: saw alerts too. KV cache miss rate jumped from 6% -> 26% on the canary hosts.
kai: any obvious kernel fallback? profiler shows more memcpy time in kernel_selector.cpp.
perf-bot: CI perf job #4821 failed: tokens/sec -15% (p95 latency +120ms). Attached flamegraph: http://ci.internal/4821/flame.html
sophia: bisect started. suspecting the scheduler priority change in PR#4821 that touched batch heuristics + kernel hinting.
ashwin: bisect narrows to merge 2471119901 (merge of scheduler-priority-refactor). Reproduces on staging with load generator.
maria: logs from staging:
```
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] scheduler.cpp: enqueue_wait=12ms, drain_wait=58ms, batch_size=3
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] continuous_batcher.cpp: kv_cache_miss=0.26, avg_queue_len=4.8
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] kernel_selector.cpp: fallback_memcpy_bytes=124MB
```
kai: kv cache hit spike should reduce memory reuse; scheduler now prefers earliest-arrival over affinity, so KV entries seldom reused -> higher miss rate.
drew: I repro'd locally with perf run: token/sec drop 17% and #small_batches up 3x. pprof shows hot path in memcpy and cudaMemcpy.
ryan: deploy-bot: canary deploy to us-west-2 started for release/2026-03-17
maria: hold the rollout. canary is already showing the token/sec regression. tagging SRE and perf.
sophia: working on a minimal patch: restore affinity tie-break + tweak batching max-wait to 6ms. running quick canary in staging.
ashwin: also testing a kernel-selector hint patch that forces the fast-copy path for small KV pops.
perf-bot: quick perf bench on staging with affinity revert: tokens/sec +13% vs bad canary, p95 latency -90ms. bench artifacts: http://ci.internal/4822/results
drew: opened PR 4830 with revert of priority change (small diff). Adding unit test for kv reuse.
ryan: rolling out revert to canary now.
deploy-bot: canary deploy for PR4830 started in us-west-2 :rocket:
maria: after revert canary metrics back within 3% of baseline. Holding full rollout until overnight window.
ashwin: scheduling a postmortem doc. root cause: heuristic changed tie-break that reduced KV reuse, causing memcpy-heavy kernel fallback and queueing build-up.
kai: followup: add perf regression test to CI that measures tokens/sec under synthesized KV hit patterns.
maria: thanks all. please add links to PRs and bench graphs in the postmortem thread. :thumbsup:
